paragraphs.source_en: Shōan gave the two of them traveling money and told them to flee for their lives; then he entrusted Konomi with a letter and put her aboard a warship departing from Sakai. The letter was addressed to Kamiya Sōtan and Shimai Sōshitsu. Shōan did not tell Konomi what the letter contained. But Konomi could imagine it: he surely wanted Sō Yoshitoshi and Konishi Yukinaga to make peace with Korea as soon as possible. Toyotomi Hideyoshi had summoned Kamiya and Shimai to Nagoya, ostensibly to join him for tea but actually to serve as his advisers.

paragraphs.source_en: The vessel on which Konomi had secured passage was a ten-sailed ship called the Kishū-maru. Its sailors and helmsmen were all newly recruited, and there were some eighty others aboard besides. A ten-sailed ship could normally carry no more than eighty people, yet few such vessels remained in any harbor; the commonest were six-sailed ships with room for only thirty.
